question: How much does it cost to refinish hardwood floors?
title: Cost to Refinish Hardwood Floors (2026)
h1: What Does Refinishing Hardwood Floors Cost?
description: Hardwood floor refinishing runs $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026; a typical whole-home job costs $800-$3,200.
capsule: Refinishing hardwood floors runs $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft in Sarasota and Manatee County in 2026, close to HomeGuide's national range of $2-$8 per sq ft. A typical whole-home job costs $800-$3,200. Dustless refinishing, recommended for occupied homes, runs $5-$8 per sq ft nationally per Angi.

sections.h2: What refinishing hardwood floors costs in 2026
sections.html:
Sand-and-refinish work on hardwood in Sarasota and Manatee County runs $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft, covering sanding down to bare wood, staining if you're changing color, and two to three coats of finish. That lines up closely with HomeGuide's 2026 national figures of $2-$8 per sq ft, with a typical whole-home job landing between $800 and $3,200 depending on square footage and finish choice.

For a rough sense of scale, an 1,800 sq ft home with hardwood in the main living areas typically lands between $8,100 and $12,600 at our local rate, before any plank replacement or stain color change is added in. We quote actual square footage from a walkthrough rather than a phone estimate, since closets, stairs and cut-in edges around cabinetry all add labor time that a flat per-room number misses.

sections.h2: What changes the price per square foot
sections.html:
Square footage isn't the only variable. A floor with deep pet scratches or dark stain that needs to come out entirely takes more passes with coarser grit before the finish sanding, which adds labor time. Switching from an existing oil-based finish to water-based, or adding a custom stain color instead of a clear coat, both add cost over a straightforward clean-and-recoat. Stairs, closets and tight corners around cabinetry also slow the job down compared to open floor, since the drum sander can't reach those spots and they have to be hand-sanded - see our separate stair tread cost guide if stairs are part of the project.

Wear layer thickness on engineered hardwood matters here too - a floor with only a 2mm wear layer left has less room for a full sanding, and in some cases a screen-and-recoat (a lighter surface pass that doesn't remove much wood) is the safer option instead of a full sand-down. Read more in our guide to wear layer thickness.

sections.h2: Is dustless refinishing worth paying more for?
sections.html: Dustless systems attach a vacuum directly to the sanding equipment and run $5-$8 per sq ft nationally per Angi, above standard sanding. For a house you're living in during the work, the difference is real - a standard sand job can leave fine dust settling for days afterward, especially with central air recirculating it through the house. If you can vacate the home during sanding, or you're doing an unoccupied rental turnover, standard sanding at the lower end of the range is often the more practical choice. We walk through both options at the estimate and let the household's schedule, not just the price gap, drive the decision.

sections.h2: What's included in a refinishing quote
sections.html: Our written estimates break refinishing into sanding, staining (if applicable), and finish coats as separate lines, plus any plank replacement needed for boards too damaged to sand through our floor repair service - that's priced separately at $95-$225 per plank. We also note dry time up front: an oil-based finish needs up to 30 days to fully cure before rugs and furniture go back, which matters for scheduling around guests or a home sale. Start with a free estimate and we'll walk the floor with you before quoting. If you're comparing refinishing against a full replacement, ask for both numbers on the same visit so you're working from real square footage rather than a rough online estimate.

faqs.q: Does refinishing cost less than replacing the floor?
faqs.a: Almost always. Refinishing at $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft is a fraction of new hardwood installed at $9-$20 per sq ft, as long as the existing floor has enough wood left to sand safely.

faqs.q: How much does replacing a few damaged planks cost before refinishing?
faqs.a: Plank replacement runs $95-$225 per plank. We typically replace damaged boards first, then sand the whole floor together so the new and old wood finish to a consistent color.

faqs.q: Does the cost change for engineered hardwood versus solid?
faqs.a: The labor is similar, but engineered floors have less wood to remove before hitting the core, so we check wear layer thickness before quoting a full sand versus a lighter screen-and-recoat.
